_population: starting_population = adults a new game starts with (never more than the starting homes hold). population_growth_seconds = seconds between groups of adults moving in from outside at normal move-in speed (happiness growth_speeds move_in); 0 = nobody moves in. move_in_group_size = most adults who arrive together each time (fewer when fewer jobs are open). move_in_only_for_jobs = newcomers are migrant workers: they only come while a post is open that nobody here can take (plan.md 5.6). move_in_needs_home = they also need room in a real home; false = they come anyway and live in Makeshift Huts until homes are built, which lowers the Housing need. The village also grows through births.
_life: Births, children and deaths (plan.md 5.6). birth_rate_per_hour = babies per adult per hour (times the move-in speed from happiness; only while a family, in a house or a hut, has a free child place: children_per_household each). Children don't work; they grow up into adults after grow_up_hours. Babies born in the same child_group_hours form one age group. death_rate_per_hour = share of adults and of children who die each hour. PLACEHOLDERS.
_housing: Households and wealth (plan.md 5.18). A household = up to adults_per_household adults + children_per_household children. wealth_classes, poorest first: an adult's class comes from their wage per hour (the highest from_wage it reaches; no job = 0 = Broke); a household's class is its adults' class. A household can afford a home when its rent is at most rent_share of the household's wages. PLACEHOLDERS.
_trade: The Trading Post's trader (plan.md 5.22): it pays sell_share of an item's normal price (plan.md 5.12) when you sell to it, and charges buy_share when you buy from it. Selling pays sales tax. PLACEHOLDERS.
_items: item_categories = the kinds of items (resources.json "category") and their names on screen. Stores sell the categories in their "sells" list (buildings.json); the Food need counts only food.
_happiness: Village happiness (plan.md 5.6 'Needs & happiness'): Food, Jobs and Housing needs, mixed by weights (shares of their total) into one 0-1 score. food_scores = score for 0, 1, 2, ... or more different foods selling at a staffed store (the last number = that many or more; variety counts, plan.md 5.21). Jobs = share of adults with a job. Housing = share of households with a real home (homeless households in huts lower it). homeless_penalty = on top of that, per_household is taken off the score for every household living in a hut, at most max (shares of 1). Needs only count from needs_from_population people (below that, happiness is 100%) and after a new village's first grace_hours. growth_speeds: for each happiness band (from = lowest score of the band), speed = the birth speed (1 = normal, 0 = no babies), move_in = the speed job seekers move in (1 = one group every population_growth_seconds, 0 = nobody comes; same as speed if left out; today: nobody at 20% or less, above that only the open jobs decide) and leave_per_hour = share of people (adults and children alike) who leave the island each hour. leave_group_size = people leave in groups this big (adults and children each in their own groups). PLACEHOLDERS.
_save: The game saves to user://save.json every autosave_seconds, right after player actions, and when it closes or goes to the background (plan.md 8). The Welcome back window shows at start-up when the game was closed for at least welcome_back_after_seconds.
_roads: Roads (plan.md 5.20). price = dollars per road tile, paid at once, ready at once; removing is free, nothing paid back. Buildings with workers need a road linked to City Hall (road_hub in buildings.json) on a tile beside one of their sides (a 2x2 building has 8 such tiles), or they get no workers. starting_roads = road tiles a new game starts with [x, y]. PLACEHOLDERS.
_construction: Building and upgrading (plan.md 5.15). Every building's materials (buildings.json) are its Level 1 amounts; each level needs level_growth times the level below (2 = doubles: Level 2 = 2x, Level 3 = 4x, Level 4 = 8x). The materials are items (resources.json, category building_material, with their base price): the warehouse's own are used first, the rest is bought from an in-game supplier when the work starts, at today's market price: the base price (dollars) plus or minus up to price_swing (0.2 = 20%), a new price every price_change_seconds. Labor = construction workers from your Construction Offices: crew of them to build anything with materials (a building can set its own crew), crew_per_level more for each upgrade level (1, then 2 for Level 2, 3 for Level 3, 4 for Level 4); they are busy until the work is done, so more offices or bigger ones let you build more at once. Paid once, labor_share of the materials' value at today's prices (0.1 = 10%; warehouse materials count too). level_seconds = how long it takes: building (Level 1), then each upgrade (to Level 2, 3, 4, ...; levels past the list take the last time). All PLACEHOLDERS.
_refunds: Share given back (0-1). cancel_refund_in_progress = cancelling a running batch gives back this share of the ingredients and wages of the hours not finished yet (hours already made are kept). Demolishing gives no money: every unit of material the building and its upgrades used goes back to the warehouse (plan.md 5.15).
_batch: Production batches (plan.md 5.1): the player picks how many hours a Farm, Mill or Bakery works, from 1 to max_hours (fewer if the Warehouse's ingredients or the cash for the wages run out). default_hours = what the panel offers first. All the ingredients and wages are paid when it starts. PLACEHOLDERS.
_stats: Statistics graphs: a point is recorded every stats_sample_seconds while playing (one point covers time spent away), keeping the latest stats_history_size points (360 x 60s = 6 hours).
_money_log: Money log in the Statistics window (plan.md 5.19): money in and out is summed into one entry every money_log_minutes (time spent away = one entry), keeping the latest money_log_size entries (48 x 30 min = 24 hours).
_workers: staffing_levels = share of a building's max_workers the player can choose (8 at level 1 -> Low 4, Medium 6, High 8). New buildings start at default_staffing. worker_types: wage_per_hour = the MINIMUM wage, set by the game. A Farm, Mill or Bakery adds a wage bonus on top, chosen per batch and locked in once it starts (wage_bonuses: share of the minimum; bonus_output: the extra share of units the batch makes; new buildings offer default_bonus; plan.md 5.6). A batch pays the full crew's wages for all its hours when it starts, whatever the staffing (fewer workers just take longer). Other buildings (warehouses, shops) pay their working workers as they go, including while the game is closed; cash may go below 0 (debt). available = false types can't be hired yet (high-skilled = high school graduates, professional = college graduates; they arrive with schools). All PLACEHOLDERS.
_tax: Sales tax on Retailer sales (plan.md 5.9): progressive like income-tax brackets, on the company's sales over the last sales_tax_window_hours. Each part of a sale pays the rate of the bracket it falls in, so selling more never leaves you with less. market_fee = the Phase 4 player-market fee per trade, paid by the seller (not used yet). PLACEHOLDERS.
_pricing: Retail prices are worked out from costs (plan.md 5.12): per hour of work (one recipe), ingredients + max_workers at the minimum wage + water at its base price + the building's value (its Level 1 materials and labor at base prices) / payback_hours, divided by the units made and by (1 - typical_tax_rate). payback_hours = hours of full-staff production for a building to pay for itself. PLACEHOLDERS.
_water: The public water supply (plan.md 5.13): buildings with water_per_hour (m³) draw it while they produce; a meter records it at price_per_m3 (dollars) and the bill is charged every billing_hours (12 = one game day; unpaid = debt). tiers = extra share of the price for the part of a cycle's m³ above "from" (first 1,200 m³ per cycle normal). bill_history = past bills kept. Unlimited supply. PLACEHOLDERS.
_power: The public power grid (plan.md 5.5): City Hall's link (grid_mw in buildings.json) adds what your own plants don't cover, up to its MW. A meter records the MWh drawn at price_per_mwh (dollars) and the bill is charged every billing_hours (12 = one game day; unpaid = debt). tiers = extra share of the price for the part of a cycle's MWh above "from". bill_history = past bills kept. PLACEHOLDERS.
_retail: Supermarket selling (plan.md 5.16). price_tags: price = share of the normal (cost-based) price; speed = how much faster or slower the village buys at that price (from a demand curve: speed = 1 / price^3). variety_bonus = extra shoppers for each different product on a store's shelves beyond the first (+10% each). All PLACEHOLDERS.

island._comment: Land around the buildable plot. margin = tiles of non-buildable land around the plot; coast_roughness / coast_frequency = how wobbly the coastline is; seed picks one fixed coastline (change it for a different shape); beaches = rough share of the coast that is sand instead of rock cliff (0-1); tree_density = how thick the placeholder forests are (0-1).
